title: Plateau probing sandbox — latency smoothing experiments
content:
Goal:
- Understand the latency 'plateau' behaviour when QPS increases across the batching thresholds. Find quick knobs to smooth p95/p99 without sacrificing too much tokens/sec.

Background / hypothesis:
- We see an odd region where increasing QPS doesn't lower p50 (expected) but p95/p99 spikes and then relaxes (sustained plateau). Hypothesis: queueing/batch-formation time + intermittent KV cache misses + GPU kernel warm paths cause non-linear tails.
- Two levers to try quickly: 1) force smaller max_batch for hot models to reduce batch wait; 2) prefill / pin top-K tokens in KV cache; 3) introduce small jittered batching windows to avoid synchronized batch flush.

Testbed:
- Model: open-llama-13b-quant (local dedicated node emulation)
- Hardware: 1x A800 80GB equiv (shared dev pool)
- Inference runtime: rwinf-runtime:main @ PR #874 (linked) + local kernel selection toggles turned on
- Config knobs: max_batch_size, max_latency_ms (batch wait), kv_cache_prefill=true/false, jitter_ms=0/1/3
- Traffic generator: k6 + small python harness for controlled bursts (attached quick script below)
- Workloads: short-context (64 tokens), med-context (256 tokens), long-context (1024 tokens). Most experiments focused on med-context since plateau visible there.

Quick commands used:
- baseline run: k6 run --vus 50 --duration 5m --http-debug=0 --rps 0 script.js (script.js contains POSTs to /v1/generate with varied seq len)
- manual targeted burst: python burst_play.py --qps 120 --burst 300s --pattern poisson
- runtime tweak: curl -X POST $ADMIN/config -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","max_batch":8,"max_latency_ms":20,"kv_prefill":true}'

Raw observations (single run snapshots) — med-context (256 tokens):
- Baseline (max_batch=16, max_latency_ms=50, kv_prefill=false, jitter=0):
  QPS observed: 95 token-req/s
  p50: 48 ms  p95: 238 ms  p99: 496 ms
  GPU util: 67%  avg batch size: 12.3

- Reduce max_batch -> 8, keep other knobs:
  QPS observed: 85 token-req/s
  p50: 42 ms  p95: 128 ms  p99: 212 ms
  GPU util: 59%  avg batch size: 7.9

- Same as above but kv_prefill=true (simple prefix cache for top-16 frequent prefixes):
  QPS observed: 88 token-req/s
  p50: 40 ms  p95: 96 ms  p99: 138 ms
  GPU util: 61%  avg batch size: 8.1  kv_hit_rate: 23%

- max_batch=16, add jitter_ms=3 (stochastic batch window), kv_prefill=false:
  QPS observed: 92 token-req/s
  p50: 47 ms  p95: 110 ms  p99: 172 ms
  GPU util: 65%  avg batch size: 11.6

- Lower max_latency_ms=20 (more aggressive flush), max_batch=16, kv_prefill=false:
  QPS observed: 90 token-req/s
  p50: 44 ms  p95: 140 ms  p99: 260 ms

Interpretation:
- The plateau/tail seems strongly correlated with average batch size crossing ~10-12; large batches reduce p50 but increase variance in p95/p99 due to occasional long queueing + kernel/alloc overheads on large B.
- Turning on small jitter (3 ms) collapsed a lot of the tail without a big throughput hit — seems to de-synchronize arrivals and avoid pathological simultaneous flushes.
- Prefill KV cache gave a surprising improvement to p95/p99 (kv_hit_rate ~ 20–25%) with negligible QPS loss — probably avoids early token-generation overheads (memory page faults / index lookups) on some common prefixes.
- Aggressive batch flush (lower max_latency_ms) reduced avg tail in some runs but sometimes increased p99: likely because flushes triggered small micro-batches during bursts causing GPU inefficiency and CPU-side overhead for many small kernels.

Mini table (med-context, aggregated of 3 runs each, median values):
- config: default (mb=16, ml=50, kv=false) -> p95 238 ms, p99 496 ms, qps 95
- config: mb=8, ml=50, kv=false -> p95 128 ms, p99 212 ms, qps 85
- config: mb=8, ml=50, kv=true -> p95 96 ms, p99 138 ms, qps 88
- config: mb=16, ml=50, jitter=3, kv=false -> p95 110 ms, p99 172 ms, qps 92

ASCII quick chart (p95 across effective avg batch size):
  avgBatch:  4   6   8    10    12    14    16
  p95(ms):  72  84  98   135   220   270   238
(note: the bump at 16 sometimes lower than 14 due to variance between runs; trend is non-monotonic)

Actionable takeaways (short):
- For med-context workloads, prefer moderate max_batch (~8) + small jitter (1–3ms) as default policy for p95-sensitive customers.
- Offer kv_prefill as an opt-in optimization for common prompt templates (low cost, measurable tail reduction).
- Beware forcing too-aggressive flush thresholds; they can make many micro-batches and increase kernel churn.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Repeat with long-context (1024) — initial micro-runs show even stronger tail due to KV misses and long-kernel spikes.
- Measure CPU-side GC/paging during tail events to confirm paging hypothesis. Add perf counters (page-faults, mmap stats).
- Explore dynamic adaptive batch cap based on recent p95 signal (auto downscale when tail drift detected).
- Benchmark with two-model cascade (small fast model fallback) to see impact on tail during bursts.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Push a small test harness to infra: run 6-hour continuous mixing poisson + diurnal to see real-world plateaus (ticket INF-1324).
- Add kv_prefill config flag into runtime admin API if we keep testing positive results. PR #874 touches batching logic so watch for merge conflicts.
- Share this doc with Rae and link into the canary run board (confluence TBD).

Appendix: small helper script (pseudo) used for burst play:
- burst_play.py (concept):
  - generate arrivals using poisson lam; send POSTs with varied seq len; sleep jitter; record latencies client-side; emit p50/p95/p99 every 30s.

Client latency capture snippet (k6-like):
  http.post(url, payload, {tags: {seq: "256"}});

End.
